headline_marked: [[Humanoid robots shatter Usain Bolt's 100m record]], Tiangong Ultra logs 9.39s sprint
headline: Humanoid robots shatter Usain Bolt's 100m record, Tiangong Ultra logs 9.39s sprint
summary: Tiangong Ultra ran the 100m in 9.39 seconds, 0.19 seconds faster than Bolt's 9.58s. Honor's Lightning also beat the record at 9.47 seconds, though both robots crashed into foam pads after the finish line.
details: Two Chinese humanoid robots have officially surpassed Usain Bolt's 100-meter dash record. Tiangong Ultra achieved a time of 9.39 seconds, while Honor's Lightning finished in 9.47 seconds, both faster than Bolt's 9.58-second record from 2009. Tiangong Ultra averaged 23.83 mph (38.34 kph) during its record-breaking sprint.

These records were set at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, an annual event. The achievement is particularly notable given that these are autonomously running bipedal robots, a more challenging form factor compared to wheeled or quadrupedal machines.

The teams behind these robots have made significant progress in a short time. Tiangong Ultra, which won the 100-meter race last year, completed it in 21.50 seconds. This year's 9.39-second time represents a reduction of over 12 seconds in just one year, a stark contrast to the nearly 100 years it took humans to shave a little over a second off the world record.

Despite their impressive speed, the robots still lack the finesse of human runners. After crossing the finish line, both the Ultra and Lightning slammed directly into foam pads, with the Lightning reportedly losing control and falling. A third robot also crumpled into the cushion, highlighting the need for improved deceleration and stopping mechanisms.

The five-day event features 51 other competitions, including boxing, football, dancing, and industrial-task contests, with 2,056 robots from 666 teams representing 16 countries. While these robots are not yet ready for widespread industrial or commercial deployment, events like this demonstrate their rapidly expanding capabilities. However, the two fastest robots are unlikely to be available in the U.S. due to the FCC's ban on foreign-made robots.

headline_marked: [[PlayStation blackout called]] for August 23-30 to protest Sony's end of physical games
headline: PlayStation blackout called for August 23-30 to protest Sony's end of physical games
summary: A community group is urging PlayStation users to log out or turn off consoles for a week, protesting Sony's plan to cease physical game production by 2028.
details: A community group, DoesItPlay, has called for a one-week PlayStation boycott from August 23 to 30. This protest targets Sony's decision to end physical game production by 2028, urging players to turn off consoles or log out of PSN.

Many in the community are skeptical about the protest's impact, noting the chosen week is ordinary with no major PlayStation events. Some suggest more drastic actions, like mass PSN subscription cancellations, would be more effective than a time-limited blackout.

The move highlights a broader industry shift towards digital-only releases, where 'buying' games often means licensing, not ownership. GOG is one of the few platforms offering complete ownership with offline installers.
Sony's decision likely reflects market preferences for digital games. Consumers can influence this trend by prioritizing physical game purchases from retailers to encourage continued distribution.
